address: bech32m checksummed encoding, accept-both at RPC/SSE/CLI edges (#36)
Contributed by Ziyang (as exfer-stack) upstream to ahuman-exfer/exfer, the Exfer chain itself.
https://github.com/ahuman-exfer/exfer/pull/38

Implements the encoding called for in #36: addresses gain a checksummed presentation form while consensus, storage, and every emitted byte stay exactly as they are.

## What

`types::address` — a self-contained codec module:

- `encode(&[u8; 32], Network) -> String`: lowercase bech32m (BIP-350) over the 32-byte address hash. At this length (61-62 chars) the code guarantees detection of any error touching up to 4 characters — every single substitution and every adjacent transposition, the two failure modes raw hex silently forwards to the chain.
- `parse_any(&str, Network) -> Result<[u8; 32], AddressParseError>`: accepts either the node's own-network bech32m form or legacy 64-hex. Dispatch is structural, not probabilistic — the whitelisted HRPs contain `x`, which is not a hex digit, so the two routes cannot collide; the legacy route's acceptance set is bit-identical to the previous `hex::decode` + length-32 checks (mixed-case hex included).
- Strictness: payload exactly 32 bytes, non-zero padding bits rejected (one canonical spelling per payload), mixed case rejected, bech32 (non-m) checksums rejected, and a wrong-network address fails with a message naming both networks ("testnet address not valid on this mainnet node") rather than a generic checksum error.
- HRPs `xf` / `xft` / `xfd` for mainnet/testnet/devnet, defined once as constants and marked PROVISIONAL pending the naming decision in #36. All three are unclaimed in SLIP-0173 (the reversed Bitcoin-style family is unavailable: `tf` and `ex` are taken).
- Network identity reuses existing mechanisms only: the `testnet` cargo feature, and devnet via the #29/#32 signature-domain bind. No new global.

Accept-both at every address input edge; zero output changes:

- `rpc.rs`: `get_balance`, `get_address_utxos`, `get_address_mempool`, and the `_batch` variants. Batch dedup happens on decoded bytes, so mixed spellings of one address collapse to one entry.
- `rpc_sse.rs`: the `addresses=` subscription filter. Emitted `script_changed` events still carry hex.
- `main.rs`: the five CLI destination-address args. Pubkey, tx-id, and hash-lock params deliberately stay hex-only — several of those are covenant pubkeys, not addresses, and encoding them identically would recreate the very confusion this fixes.
- `get_script_utxos` untouched (arbitrary script param, not an address).

Shared test vectors for the ecosystem:

- `tests/vectors/address_vectors.json` — 53 vectors across 15 classes (round-trips per network, case rules, substitution/transposition, wrong variant, wrong network, payload lengths, padding, malformed, hex fallback, BIP-350 sanity), generated deterministically by the `dev-harness`-gated `gen_address_vectors` bin. Downstream consumers (walletd, the Python SDK, the wallets) vendor this file so one fixture pins every implementation. The fixture embeds the HRP map and the integration test asserts it equals the compiled constants — a future HRP change cannot leave stale vectors silently green.
